A portal can transform the surface of an entity's mesh into an entrance to another scene, allowing users to freely travel between different scenes within the application.
## Components and materials
A portal is implemented using the following components and materials:
### PortalWorldComponent
This component can convert an entity and all its child nodes into an independent world, whose contents can only be viewed through the portal. This component should be used together with `PortalComponent`, `PortalCrossingComponent`, and `PortalMaterial`.
### PortalMaterial
A type of material that can turn the surface of an entity's mesh into a portal leading to other teleportable scenes. This material should be used together with `PortalComponent`. To convert a mesh into a portal, add this material to the `ModelComponent` and mount the `PortalComponent` on the same entity.
### PortalComponent
This component enables the surface of an entity's mesh to become a portal to the target world (that is, the EC tree of `targetEntity`) and should be used together with `PortalMaterial`. This component provides the following configurable properties:
| **Property** | **Description** |
| --- | --- |
| allowClipping <br>  | When an object passing through the portal exceeds the portal's boundaries, should the portion outside the boundaries be clipped? <br>  <br> * `true`: Clip <br>    ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/482d878f56284b8c9c972d6a56e74b5a~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) <br> * `false`: Do not clip <br>    ![Image](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/c9c0a26cd9f94f2989dbfcd784947793~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) |
| allowEntityCrossing | Whether to allow entities with `PortalCrossingComponent` to pass through this portal. <br>  <br> * `true`: Allow <br> * `false`: Not allow |
| doubleSide | Whether to render both sides (front and back) of the portal. <br>  <br> * `true`: The portal and its internal world can be seen from both the front and back. <br> * `false`: The portal and its internal world cannot be seen from the back. |
| enable | Whether to enable this portal. <br>  <br> * `true`: Enable <br> * `false`: Not enable |
| targetEntity | The target entity, representing the world visible inside the portal. If `targetEntity` is `null`, the portal will not be rendered. To render the portal correctly, `targetEntity` must be set to a valid `Entity` object. |
### PortalCrossingComponent
This component enables an entity and its child nodes to traverse the portal. This component should be used together with `PortalComponent`, `PortalWorldComponent`, and `PortalMaterial`.
## Core entities
The portal is collaboratively implemented by the following three types of entities:

* `PortalEntity`: An entity with `PortalComponent` mounted;
* `PortalWorldEntity`: An entity with `PortalWorldComponent` mounted;
* `PortalCrossingEntity`: An entity with `PortalCrossingComponent` mounted.

The following structural relationships must be implemented between entities:

* `PortalEntity` must be either the parent node or sibling node of `PortalWorldEntity`, and cannot be a child node of `PortalWorldEntity`.

## Limitations
The system can maintain and render up to 8 pairs of `PortalEntity` and `PortalWorldEntity` simultaneously.
## Code sample
The following code implements a traversable 3D portal scene: a `PortalWorld` is placed in space as the world displayed on the other side of the portal, then a `PortalEntity` with material and mesh is created and bound to that world; meanwhile, a model for the traversal effect is loaded and placed into `PortalWorld`.
```Kotlin
SpatialView { content, _ ->
    // Define PortalWorld (the root node of the content to be displayed inside the portal)
    val world =
        Entity().apply {
            // Set the coordinates of PortalWorld, in this example, PortalWorld is placed on the left side of the portal
            val worldTransform = TransformComponent().apply {
            setPosition(Vector3(-0.3F, 0F, 0.2F))
            setScaleVector(Vector3(1F))
            }
            components.set(worldTransform)
            components.set(PortalWorldComponent())
        }

    // Define the portal itself
    val portalEntity = Entity().apply {
        val material = PortalMaterial()
        val mesh = MeshResource.createPanel(1.0f, 1.0f, 0.3f)
        components.set(ModelComponent(mesh, material))
        components.set(PortalComponent(world, true, true, true, true))
        components.set(TransformComponent())
        // Set the portal's coordinates and apply a deflection angle to observe the scenes on both sides of the portal
        components
            .get<TransformComponent>()!!
            .setPosition(Vector3(0F, 0F, 0.3F))
            .setRotator(Rotator(0F, 45F, 0F))
            .setScaleVector(Vector3(0.8F))
    }

    content.addEntity(world)
    content.addEntity(portalEntity)
    
    // Define the model that can cross the portal
    val willCrossing = Entity.load("asset://Portal/plane.glb").apply {
    // Set the scaling factor and rotation offset for the willCrossing model (adjust according to the actual size of the model; this coefficient is only for this model) so that the model displays correctly
    val transform = TransformComponent().apply {
        setPosition(Vector3(-0.3F, 0F, 0.2F))
        setScaleVector(Vector3(0.0005F))
        setRotator(Rotator(-90F, 45F, 0F))
    }
    components.set(transform)
    components.set(PortalCrossingComponent())
 }      
    world.addChild(willCrossing)
}
```

## API reference
For detailed descriptions of `PortalWorldComponent`, `PortalMaterial`, `PortalComponent`, and `PortalCrossingComponent`, refer to [API Reference](https://developer.picoxr.com/spatial-api/index.html).
